comments.author: @foyjamez
comments.text:
Enlist in the US Navy. Share a bunk with 2 other guys on a ship. Tiny home will seems luxurious in comparison after a WestPac.
Seriously though, you need to be a minimalist inside your tiny home, and then build exterior structures on your property afterwards. They will not appreciate in value, much like an RV, and will probably not add value to your land if you don't oversize your septic and electrical service for an eventual full-sized house with the tiny home becoming a guest cottage.
EDIT: OMG That 2nd bedroom doesn't have a emergency window exit. Definitely not a code-compliant bedroom.
EDIT 2: I know a contractor who was supposed to set a tiny home--the whole thing was a scam. The buyer sent deposits somewhere, then the "delivery guys" called and said "We're in New Mexico and need another $10k by VENMO to deliver to AZ".
EDIT 3: Most of those capsule homes don't use "listed and approved" materials, so you don't know what they are made of; do you remember that bad high sulphur drywall from China from the early 2000s?
EDIT 4: There are many cheaper manufactured/mobile homes, though they need about $25k to be installed IF you have existing utilities, much more if you decide to put a basement under them, but a used model from a park that is being shut down could save a lot of money. The tiny home will still need to be transported and craned onto a foundation and the utilities will need to be hooked up, so be prepared to add a similar amount of money to that base price.

comments.text: I have a 12x32 shed conversion to tiny cabin on remote unincorporated land in NM that I own. I think at most I spent about 30k total for the building and the work. It's not my primary place of living, I'm here about 1/3 of the year. I have standard utility power but no actual plumbing; water and waste have specific processes. You have to not be married to all the city conveniences, and not be driven to collect "things" to be satisfied. It’s only 12’x12’, but I added a loft for sleeping quarters and storage, so that nearly doubled the square footage.  I purchased a lot of the materials at a leftover inventory outlet for DIYers, which save me a ton of money.  All in, it cost me about $2,700 to build.  I estimate I could add electric, plumbing, insulation, and paneling for another $5,000 to $7,000.

Nobody should be paying 100k+ for a 300 square foot home.
